title: Windows: wren memory fetch fails with OSError: [WinError 1] Incorrect function while loading sentence-transformers model
body:
## Summary

On Windows, `wren memory fetch` fails during memory store initialization when the local sentence-transformers embedding model is loaded.

The failure happens inside `transformers -> tqdm -> sys.stderr/sys.stdout.flush()` while loading model weights.

## Environment

* OS: Windows
* Python: 3.11
* Environment: conda
* Shells tested:

  * Git Bash / MINGW64
  * Windows terminal / CMD style
* Wren command:

```bash
wren memory fetch -q "successful transaction volume in may"
```

## Error

```text
OSError: [WinError 1] Incorrect function
```

Traceback points to:

```text
wren.memory.cli.fetch
wren.memory.store.MemoryStore.__init__
wren.memory.embeddings.warm_up
lancedb.embeddings.sentence_transformers
sentence_transformers.SentenceTransformer
transformers.modeling_utils
tqdm.std.status_printer
sys.stderr.flush / sys.stdout.flush
```

There is also this warning before the crash:

```text
Warning: You are sending unauthenticated requests to the HF Hub.
Please set a HF_TOKEN to enable higher rate limits and faster downloads.
```

But the HF warning does not appear to be the root cause. The crash seems related to the transformers/tqdm progress bar while loading the local embedding model.

## Expected behavior

`wren memory fetch` should initialize the local memory store and embedding model successfully on Windows.

## Actual behavior

The command crashes with:

```text
OSError: [WinError 1] Incorrect function
```

## Workaround

This workaround works without modifying Wren source code:

```bash
python -c "from transformers.utils import logging; logging.disable_progress_bar(); logging.set_verbosity_error(); from wren.cli import app; app()" memory fetch -q "successful transaction volume in may"
```

This suggests the issue is caused by the transformers/tqdm progress bar being enabled before Wren loads the sentence-transformers embedding model.

## Possible fix

Disable transformers progress bars before warming up the embedding model, especially on Windows, or provide an official CLI option / environment-variable based workaround for Wren memory commands.

For example, Wren could call something equivalent to:

```python
from transformers.utils import logging
logging.disable_progress_bar()
```

before initializing the sentence-transformers embedding model.

linked_prs.title: fix: disable transformers progress bar on Windows
linked_prs.patch:
diff --git a/core/wren/src/wren/memory/embeddings.py b/core/wren/src/wren/memory/embeddings.py
index ef238b7ca0..e8a7b51b2b 100644
--- a/core/wren/src/wren/memory/embeddings.py
+++ b/core/wren/src/wren/memory/embeddings.py
@@ -14,12 +14,22 @@
 _DEFAULT_DIM = 384
 
 
+def _disable_transformers_progress_bar() -> None:
+    # Imported lazily: transformers ships with the optional `memory` extra,
+    # so this module must stay importable when that extra is not installed.
+    from transformers.utils import logging as transformers_logging  # noqa: PLC0415
+
+    transformers_logging.disable_progress_bar()
+
+
 def get_embedding_function(model_name: str = _DEFAULT_MODEL):
     """Return a LanceDB sentence-transformers embedding function.
 
     The returned object implements ``compute_source_embeddings(texts)``
     and ``compute_query_embeddings(query)`` used by :class:`MemoryStore`.
     """
+    _disable_transformers_progress_bar()
+
     import lancedb.embeddings  # noqa: PLC0415
 
     registry = lancedb.embeddings.get_registry()
@@ -46,6 +56,7 @@ def suppress_stderr():
 
 def warm_up(embed_fn):
     """Trigger model loading silently and return the vector dimension."""
+    _disable_transformers_progress_bar()
     with suppress_stderr():
         probe = embed_fn.compute_source_embeddings(["probe"])
     return len(probe[0])
